open_points.subject: A18 rule 1 backup look interval
open_points.text: The process looks at the clock at least once in each interval of the imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` constant (60 seconds)
open_points.question: Is the maximum gap between backup-eligibility looks measured by the monotonic clock or by UTC wall-clock time, especially when the wall clock moves?
options: Measure elapsed gaps with the monotonic clock and read UTC wall time at each eligibility look
Measure both the gap and the daily time with UTC wall-clock time
Use fixed UTC wall-clock intervals rather than a rolling maximum gap
open_points.default_guess: Use the monotonic clock to keep consecutive eligibility looks at most `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` apart, and read UTC wall time once at each look to decide the date and daily-time crossing.

witness.initial: Registry is running with service tokens; a look reads 02:59:30 UTC, and no backup for that UTC date exists.
events: The host administrator sets the UTC wall clock back ten minutes immediately after the look.
Registry continues running until the wall clock passes 03:00 again.
outcomes: A monotonic-gap scheduler continues looking at least every 60 elapsed seconds and starts the backup at its first qualifying look after the repeated 03:00.
A wall-clock-gap scheduler may wait until the wall clock reaches the prior reading plus 60 seconds, producing a materially later qualifying look and backup.
witness.observer: The owner sees the different recorded backup instant and availability time.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 1 overlapping daily runs
open_points.text: Runs never overlap: a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its own.
open_points.question: After the earlier run finishes, is the date whose 03:00 was blocked permanently skipped, or may its run start late at a subsequent qualifying look?
options: Skip that date permanently, as with a stopped or owner-only Registry at 03:00
Start that date's run at the first later look after the earlier run finishes
Mark the date missed only when an eligibility look actually occurs while the earlier run is active
open_points.default_guess: Skip the blocked date permanently and remember it as missed, because the text says its 03:00 makes no run of its own.

witness.initial: A backup run begun on 2026-11-23 is still running at 03:00 UTC on 2026-11-24; Registry remains otherwise eligible and has no kept backup dated 2026-11-24.
events: The scheduler looks immediately before and at 03:00 on 2026-11-24 and observes the earlier run.
outcomes: 2026-11-24 is permanently skipped because its 03:00 found another run active.
A 2026-11-24 run starts at 03:11 because the crossing condition, no-kept-backup condition and no-overlap condition are then all satisfied.
witness.observer: The owner sees either one or two kept backups after the earlier run finishes.

open_points.subject: A21 review of the A18 scheduling change
open_points.text:
A18 rule 1 still asks a look at the clock at least once in each interval —
the constant is the longest gap, as "at least once a minute" was — so no
rule's behaviour moved.
open_points.question: Must backup eligibility checks retain the former fixed `every BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` cadence, or may they now occur at any frequency whose longest gap is the constant?
options: Permit any cadence with a maximum gap of `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`
State explicitly that the broader cadence is intentional and that observable backup start times may change
open_points.default_guess: Treat the new A18 wording as a deliberate maximum-gap guarantee and correct A21's claim that only naming changed and no behavior moved.

witness.initial: Registry starts before 03:00, looks at 02:59:30, and has no kept backup for the date.
events: Under a fixed 60-second cadence, its next look is 03:00:30.
Under the new maximum-gap wording, it may additionally look at 02:59:59 and 03:00:00.
outcomes: The retained fixed cadence starts the backup at 03:00:30.
The newly permitted cadence starts it at 03:00:00.
witness.observer: The owner sees different recorded backup instants; A18 permits the second result while A21 says behavior did not move.

open_points.subject: A17 formal secret invariant
open_points.text: for secrets s1 != s2 in config: value(s1) != value(s2) and len >= SECRET_MIN_BYTES
open_points.question: What objects does `s1 != s2` distinguish, and whose length must `len` measure?
options: For every pair of distinct configured secret fields, their values differ, and every configured secret value has length at least `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` UTF-8 bytes
Apply the length clause to both `s1` and `s2` inside every pair
Apply the length clause only to one unspecified secret in each pair
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite it as two explicit invariants: every configured secret value has at least `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` UTF-8 bytes, and every two distinct configured secret fields have unequal values.

open_points.subject: A17 Required tests for the secret invariant
open_points.text:
Two services with one token stop the start, and so does each other pair
of equal secrets: a token and the owner credential, a token and the
backup key, the owner credential and the backup key.
open_points.question: Does the test have to exercise every unordered pair of the four service-token fields and every token-to-owner/token-to-backup pair, or only one representative service token for each stated category?
options: Test one representative token for each category
Test every unordered pair of configured secret fields
Use a parameterized test whose cases explicitly enumerate every configured secret-field pair
open_points.default_guess: Require every unordered pair of configured secret fields, preferably through an explicitly enumerated parameterized test.

open_points.subject: A17 Required tests for minimum secret length
open_points.text:
For each kind of secret — a service
token, the owner credential and the backup key — a value one byte shorter
than `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` stops the start and one of exactly
`SECRET_MIN_BYTES` bytes is accepted.
open_points.question: Does “a service token” require the boundary result to be shown for each of the four service-token fields, or for one representative token only?
options: Each of the four service-token fields
One shared validation-path test plus an explicit check that every service-token field uses that path
open_points.default_guess: Require the boundary result for every service-token field, owner credential and backup key, because the invariant applies to every configured secret.
